items.title: fix: add ignore_mismatched_sizes option to model loader
items.bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #10416

## Problem

When loading certain models (e.g. GLM-OCR / GLM4V variants with GQA), `from_pretrained` fails with a `RuntimeError: size mismatch` even though the checkpoint is valid. This happens because LLaMA-Factory does not pass `ignore_mismatched_sizes` to the model loader, causing transformers (>=5.0 with strict shape checking) to reject otherwise-loadable weights.

## Solution

Add an `ignore_mismatched_sizes` boolean argument to `BaseModelArguments` (defaults to `False` to preserve existing behaviour). When set to `True`, the flag is forwarded to `AutoModel*.from_pretrained`, allowing transformers to skip shape-mismatch errors.

Users opt in via their YAML config or CLI flag:
```yaml
ignore_mismatched_sizes: true
```

This mirrors the existing pattern already used in `quantization.py` for MXFP4/FP8 quantized models.

## Testing

- Verified that the new field is picked up by the dataclass argument parser.
- Existing load path is unchanged when `ignore_mismatched_sizes` is `False` (default).

items.title: fix(data): GLM4-MOE tool_extractor never overridden, round-trip fails
items.bodyExcerpt:
## What does this PR do?

`GLM4MOEToolUtils` overrides `tool_formatter`/`function_formatter` to produce its own XML-ish format (`<tool_call>{name}\n<arg_key>...</arg_key>\n<arg_value>...</arg_value>...`, matching `GLM4_MOE_TOOL_PROMPT`), but never overrides `tool_extractor` — it inherits `QwenToolUtils.tool_extractor`, which does `json.loads()` on the `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` body. That body is never valid JSON for this format, so extraction always fails and falls through to returning the raw, unparsed string instead of `list[FunctionCall]`.

Separately, `function_formatter` never emitted the closing `</tool_call>` tag that `GLM4_MOE_TOOL_PROMPT` itself documents (`"\n...\n</tool_call>\n"`), which the new extractor needs to delimit consecutive tool calls when the model emits more than one.

```python
tu = get_tool_utils("glm4_moe")
formatted = tu.function_formatter([FunctionCall("get_weather", '{"city": "Paris"}')])
tu.tool_extractor(formatted)
# before: returns the same raw string unchanged (not parsed)
# after:  [FunctionCall(name='get_weather', arguments='{"city": "Paris"}')]
```

Confirmed this is live, registered code: `"glm4_moe"` is in the `TOOLS` registry and wired into multiple real templates in `src/llamafactory/data/template.py` — not experimental/dead code. Any chat inference using a glm4_moe-family template with tool calling currently cannot parse the model's own generated tool calls back into structured `FunctionCall`s.

## Fix

- Add a `tool_extractor` override to `GLM4MOEToolUtils`, mirroring the regex-based extraction pattern already used by sibling classes (`MiniMaxM2ToolUtils`/`Qwen35ToolUtils`) for their own XML-ish formats: match `<tool_call>NAME ... </tool_call>` blocks, then pull `<arg_key>/<arg_value>` pairs out of each block (with a `json.loads` attempt per value, falling back to the raw string — same convention as the sibling extractors).
- Add the missing closing `</tool_call>` tag in `function_formatter`.

items.title: [Bug]: _compute_slot_mapping_kernel reads block_table out of bounds for cache groups whose block table is narrower than the sequence
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

`_compute_slot_mapping_kernel` in `vllm/v1/worker/block_table.py` masks its block-table load by
token validity and CP ownership, but **not** by whether the computed column index is inside the
row. Any KV cache group whose block table does not span the sequence in raw token positions
therefore performs an unbounded out-of-bounds read, scaling with sequence length.

On 8× MI325X (gfx942, ROCm 7.2.3) this eventually crosses into an unmapped page and takes down
every rank with `Memory access fault by GPU node-N ... Reason: Unknown`.

### The missing guard

`vllm/v1/worker/block_table.py` @ `main` `94d96e24`:

```python
block_indices = (                                    # :463-466
    virtual_block_indices * BLOCKS_PER_KV_BLOCK
    + local_block_offsets // block_size
)
block_numbers = tl.load(                             # :467-471
    block_table_ptr + row_offset + block_indices,
    mask=mask & is_local,                            # :469  ← no range term
    other=0,
).to(tl.int64)
slot_offsets = local_block_offsets % block_size
slot_ids = block_numbers * block_size + slot_offsets
slot_ids = tl.where(is_local, slot_ids, PAD_ID)      # :474  ← no range term
```

The model-side QSA slot helpers in #53896 do bound this (`valid &= logical_blocks < block_table.shape[1]`
and a clamp before indexing); the generic kernel is the one path we found that does not.

### Two independent instances, both from in-flight model PRs

Neither spec class is on `main` yet; both are added by open PRs, and each declares a
**one-block-per-request** side cache that the kernel then indexes with **raw token positions**:

| PR | spec | `max_num_blocks_per_req()` | effective row width | index computed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #53896 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) | `CircularBufferSpec` | `1` | 128 tokens (after the 128-token alignment in `get_block_table_width`) | `pos // 8` |
| #53906 (GLM-5.3-Flash) | `KpoolTailSpec` | `1` | 128 tokens | `pos // index_kpool` |

items.title: [Bug]: Assistant `content=null` + `tool_calls` renders literal "None" into chat template context — degenerate outputs in agent workloads
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Environment
- vLLM: `v0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187` (also present on recent mainline `dev` builds)
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash (any GLM chat template that emits per-turn `<think>` and renders `{{ content }}` for assistant turns; the keys/GLM stock `chat_template.jinja` is affected)
- Hardware: 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), TP4
- Client: pi agent (any agent harness sending `content: null` + `tool_calls` assistant turns — standard OpenAI agent format; cursor/openai-python do the same)

### Symptom
Long agent sessions (multi-turn tool calling) intermittently produce **degenerate repetitive outputs** (e.g. an infinite loop of `# --` or a single reasoning loop consuming the entire `max_tokens` budget with zero content tokens). Probability increases with the number of tool-call turns in history.

### Root cause
When an agent client sends an assistant message with `content: null` and `tool_calls`, the message passes through to `apply_chat_template` with `content=None`. The GLM chat template renders this turn as:

```
<|assistant|><think></think>None<tool_call>bash<arg_key>...
                       ^^^^ literal "None"
```

Verified with `tokenizer.apply_chat_template` (transformers 4.5x):

```python
msgs = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "check metrics"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": None, "tool_calls": [...]},   # agent turn
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c0", "content": "run=3"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "continue"},
]
tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tools=tools, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
# → '<|assistant|><think></think>None<tool_call>bash...'
#    with content="" instead of None:
# → '<|assistant|><think></think><tool_call>bash...'   (clean)
```

Every tool-calling turn injects one literal `None` token-sequence into the context. After 8-20 turns (a normal agent session) the model's in-context pattern degrades and reasoning collapses into repetition loops.

items.title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer overwrites its own KV cache: backend advertises a kernel block size the kernels do not use
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

On ROCm, the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool sparse indexer **silently overwrites its own KV cache**. 4096 pool entries are written into 864 distinct slots, so ~79 % of the indexer's keys are wrong. The model still produces fluent text, so nothing crashes — long-context recall just degrades, and `temperature=0` stops being reproducible because the damage depends on which physical blocks the allocator hands out.

This is **ROCm-only** and distinct from #40018 (whose fix, #43781, is present in the tree I tested).

### Root cause

`DeepseekV32IndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):

```python
return [1, MultipleOf(16)] if current_platform.is_rocm() else [64]
```

On CUDA the backend declares exactly `[64]`, so vLLM sets `kernel_block_size = 64`, `BlockTable.use_hybrid_blocks = True`, and builds a kernel-granular block table. On ROCm it declares "any multiple of 16", so the hybrid aligner's choice (640 tokens here) is taken as natively supported: `blocks_per_kv_block == 1`, **no kernel-granular block table**.

But the kernels do not read 640-token blocks. DeepGEMM/AITER paged-MQA reads pool pages of 32 states; with `tokens_per_state == index_kpool == 4` that is 128 tokens. So the storage block (640 tok = 160 states) is five pages, and both `slot_mapping` and `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` address it with the **page** size (32) while the block table holds **spec-block** ids — a 5x over-subscription.

The intended split is even documented in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py` as `storage_kernel_block_size`, but that identifier appears nowhere else in the tree — it was never implemented.

### Evidence (8x MI350X, gfx950, TP8, ROCm 7.2.3, `index_kpool=4`, `block_size=640`)

Instrumented at the indexer, two identical requests, prefix caching off:

| | before | after fix |
|---|---|---|
| distinct cache slots written (of 4096 pools) | **864** | **4096** |
| `max_slot` | 863 (= 26x32+31) | 4159 (= 26x

items.title: [Perf][ROCm] Sparse-MLA/kpool backends fall back to rebuilding attention metadata per draft step, capping useful MTP depth at k=4
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

On ROCm with GLM-5.3-Flash, vLLM logs at startup:

```
Fused multi-step draft decode is not supported by attention backend(s)
DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER, KPOOL_TAIL, ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE;
falling back to rebuilding attention metadata between draft steps.
```

Because the metadata is rebuilt between every draft step, the per-step cost of MTP speculation is high enough that deeper speculation stops paying for itself well before the draft quality runs out. Measurements below quantify the gap.

### Measurements

8x MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, TP8, GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, `--max-model-len 1048576`, 2 000-token context, 256 output tokens, unique per-request prefixes (nothing hits the prefix cache), warmup round then median of 3-4 rounds.

| `num_speculative_tokens` | acceptance length | draft acceptance rate | 1 user | 16 users | 64 users |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2.57 | 78.4 % | 155 tok/s | 1 432 | 3 012 |
| **4** | **3.36** | 58.9 % | **173** | **1 499** | **3 055** |
| 6 | 3.76 | 46.0 % | 175 | 1 367 | 2 874 |

The accepted length keeps climbing (2.57 → 3.36 → 3.76), i.e. the draft head still has useful signal at k=6. But throughput peaks at k=4 and *falls* at k=6, which is what you would expect when each additional draft step carries a fixed metadata-rebuild cost rather than being fused.

Note this model has `num_nextn_predict_layers = 1`, so every draft token is another autoregressive pass through the same MTP head — the per-step overhead is paid k times.

### Why this matters

For latency-sensitive single-stream use, speculation is the main lever (at high concurrency the GPU is compute-saturated and speculation contributes almost nothing — see the 64-user column). Being capped at k=4 by framework overhead rather than by draft quality leaves measurable throughput on the table.

Is fused multi-step draft decode feasible for these backends (`ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`, `DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER`, `KPOOL_TAIL`), or is there a structural reason the sparse-in

items.title: [ROCm] Fused shared experts unavailable for GLM-5.3-Flash: Fp8Config not handled by the FSE gate, and glm5next never wires it
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

GLM-5.3-Flash has `n_shared_experts = 1`, but AITER fused shared experts (FSE) cannot be used with it for two independent reasons. The first is a one-line gate I have a working patch for; the second is model wiring that needs an MTP-aware decision.

### 1. `Fp8Config` is not handled by the FSE compatibility gate

`is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` (`model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/config_utils.py`) special-cases `DeepseekV4FP8Config` and `QuarkConfig`, then falls through to:

```
shared-expert FSE quantization compatibility is not implemented for Fp8Config
```

For a plain fp8 checkpoint this looks safe to allow. `Fp8Config` applies one global `weight_block_size` and one activation scheme to everything it covers, so the routed and shared experts carry the same scheme by construction — the only way they can diverge is if exactly one side sits in `ignored_layers`. GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8 has `weight_block_size: [128, 128]`, `activation_scheme: dynamic`, `ignored_layers: null`.

```python
    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.fp8 import Fp8Config

    if isinstance(quant_config, Fp8Config):
        from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import (
            is_layer_skipped,
        )

        ignored = quant_config.ignored_layers or []
        experts_skipped = is_layer_skipped(expert_prefix, ignored, match_mode="suffix")
        shared_skipped = is_layer_skipped(
            shared_expert_prefix, ignored, match_mode="suffix"
        )
        if experts_skipped != shared_skipped:
            side = shared_expert_prefix if shared_skipped else expert_prefix
            return False, (
                f"fp8 quantization covers only one side of the fusion ({side} "
                "is in ignored_layers)"
            )
        return True, None
```

With this the gate opens and the warning disappears. Happy to send it as a PR on its own if you want it independent of the rest.

### 2. `models/glm5next/` does not wire

items.title: Fix Qwen3.5 rope validation TypeError: list | set (#36920)
Combined configuration of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP), fp8 KV cache, and AITER's Shuffle KV (SKV) layout
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose
Bring up the combined configuration of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP), fp8 KV cache, and AITER's Shuffle KV (SKV) layout in vLLM on ROCm. The three features had each been validated in isolation, but had not been run together end-to-end.

Related issue:
During integration, we uncovered an issue making ROCM_AITER_FA unusable as an MTP drafter at concurrency > 1. When running the MTP drafter with ROCM_AITER_FA, the metadata builder initialized the quantization scale as a scalar instead of the required [num_blocks, num_kv_heads, block_size] tensor. At low concurrency this was masked (HIP path), but at higher concurrency dispatch switched to ASM, causing out-of-bounds reads and SIGSEGV across TP workers.

**Changes:**
1. **Direct routing in the decode forward path** – In `AiterFlashAttentionImpl.forward`, the multi-token decode branch (`decode_max_query_len > 1` AND `is_shuffle_kv_cache_enabled()`) now bypasses `paged_attention_common` and calls `aiter.pa_fwd_asm` directly. This is necessary because `paged_attention_common`'s CU-count heuristic can select the HIP kernel for small batches, which has `mtp=1` hardcoded and silently processes only the first query token.
2. **Wrapper API extensions in `_aiter_ops.py`** – `rocm_aiter_ops.pa_fwd_asm` and `rocm_aiter_ops.paged_attention_common` now forward `max_qlen` and `qo_indptr` (and `high_precision` for the dispatcher) to the underlying AITER functions, which already accepted them.
3. Fix scale allocation for drafter – Introduced shared _maybe_allocate_shuffle_scale() and applied it to both build() and build_for_drafting() so the drafter correctly provides the expected FP8 shuffle scale tensor. Change is gated and has no impact on non-SKV paths.


## Test Commands & Benchmark Setup

All runs use **GLM-4.7-FP8** and **MTP=2** on 4 GPUs (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7`). Only the attention backend / KV-cache layout changes between runs.

Four backends were evaluated: **ROCM_AITER_FA (RAFA)**, **ROCM_AIT

FIX #48380

Two DSpark fixes for DSA-family targets:

1. **Draft cache dtype.** With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` the DSpark draft — a dense (non-MLA) Qwen3-style transformer — inherited the target's `cache_config` and tried to use the MLA-only fp8_ds_mla layout, which no dense attention backend accepts (`ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda ...`). `load_dspark_model` now falls back to the model dtype for the draft's KV cache; the draft cache is a few dense layers, so the memory cost is negligible.
2. **DCP fail-fast.** The DFlash/DSpark draft slot mapping is DCP-blind (`ctx_pos // block_size`), so with `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` the draft reads wrong KV blocks and acceptance silently collapses to ~0% (reported by @Leoyzen in #46514). Config validation now rejects the combination instead of degrading silently.

**Not a duplicate:** #47934 (FP4 target on B300) and #47626 (H20 fp8) crash later, in FlashInfer draft attention; no open PR touches the draft cache-config inheritance or adds a DCP guard for dflash/dspark.

**Testing** (4×H200, GLM-5.2-NVFP4 target, RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark):
- Before: the repro from #48380 fails at draft load with the ValueError above.
- After: server boots, output coherent end-to-end; 95 tok/s N=1, 341 tok/s aggregate N=8, mean accepted length ~2.4 (metrics: 4065 accepted / 2999 drafts / 20993 draft tokens).
- DCP guard: same command + `--decode-context-parallel-size 2` now fails at config validation with a clear NotImplementedError (previously: silent ~0% acceptance).

AI assistance was used for this change (Claude); the submitter reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

items.title: [Spec Decode] DFlash/DSpark draft support under decode context parallelism
items.bodyExcerpt:
### What

Make dense (GQA/MHA) DFlash/DSpark drafts work under `decode_context_parallel_size > 1`
by caching the whole DCP group's KV heads on every rank.

Rebased on `main` after #52188. That PR landed the DCP-aware draft slot mapping this
branch used to carry (`cp_local_slot` / `prepare_dcp_local_seq_lens` in
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cp_utils.py`), and its version is strictly better: it also handles
the null block and the rejected context suffix. That commit is dropped here in favour
of upstream's, leaving the part #52188 does not cover.

#52188 enables the MLA draft path (Kimi-K3, one latent KV head, no head-gather). This
PR enables the dense path, where the head-gather is exactly what breaks.

### Why (root cause)

Reported by @Leoyzen in #46514: DFlash/DSpark acceptance collapses to ~0% under DCP.

The dense flash DCP path (`_forward_with_dcp`: all-gather query heads across the DCP
group, attend against the rank-local KV shard, LSE-merge) is only correct when a rank's
KV shard holds the KV heads for all gathered query heads, i.e. KV heads replicated
across the DCP group. `verify_with_parallel_config` enforces this for dense *targets*;
nothing checked the *draft*. The GLM-5.2 DSpark draft is MHA (64q/64kv), so under TP4
each rank has a 16-head shard and the gathered 64 query heads are GQA-remapped 4:1 onto
the wrong KV heads.

### How

Cache the whole DCP group's KV heads on every rank (replicated) for that rank's
interleaved positions:

- `cache_num_kv_heads` decouples the KV-cache spec from the impl's head count
  (`Attention.__init__`, defaults to `num_kv_heads`, only larger for this case).
- The draft precompute all-gathers K/V across the DCP group in the same rank order the
  query gather uses, so MHA maps 1:1 and GQA stays contiguous.
- The query block's K/V is not slotted into such a cache: the DCP path attends it
  against the freshly computed K/V, and at input-prep time the rank holds only its
  local heads, so writing them would corrupt the replicated layou

items.title: [Quantization][ModelOpt] Serve modelopt_mixed checkpoints with FP8_PB layers
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Serves `modelopt_mixed` checkpoints containing FP8_PB layers. Rebased onto #49381.

FP8_PB and FP8_PB_WO are the same quantization scheme — per-block FP8 with dynamic
per-token activation quant — resolving to the same QuantKey pair and the same block-FP8
kernel. They differ only in scale serialization: FP8_PB_WO exports ModelOpt's 4-D
`weight_scale` [out_blk, 1, in_blk, 1], which requires every partition to be
block-aligned; FP8_PB uses DeepSeek's 2-D `weight_scale_inv`, sized by ceiling division,
so a partition may end in a partial block.

GLM-5.2 needs the latter. `q_a_proj` (2048) + `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` (576) fuse to a
2624-wide `fused_qkv_a_proj`; `2624 % 128 = 64`, and the layer is replicated, so no TP
degree makes it block-aligned. Previously this failed with
`KeyError: '...weight_scale_inv'`.

## Design

Since the layout can't live in the QuantKey, it rides on `CkptCtx.block_scale_deepseek`
— the per-checkpoint carrier #49381 already provides — and `KFp8Block128` branches on it.
`FormatScheme` is the wrong seam: it composes *around* the key schemes and can't replace
what the weight scheme registers, and a secondpossible for the
same key.

Adding FP8_PB is one `LINEAR_ALGOS` row plus one `resolve()` row. No new sub-config —
`resolve()` only reads `subcfg` for the NVFP4 LinearKernel`
already reads whichever scale name is present, so no kernel change.

`kFp8Static128BlockSym` is 128x128, so a checkpoint declaring another `group_size` is
rejected at config time rather than silently m

## Two fixes to existing behavior

1. `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig` never implems()`, which
   `VllmConfig` uses to enable `+quant_fp8`. Without it `QuantFP8` runs `forward_native`,
   emitting unpacked fp32 group scales where Dwants them
   UE8M0-packed into int32 — the model serves NaN logits. Resolving it per layer fixes
   FP8_PB_WO mixed checkpoints too, not just F

2. `deep_gemm_warmup` discovered layers via `ip8LinearMethod)

items.title: [Model Loader][Perf] Auto-prefetch VirtioFS checkpoints
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enable RAM-guarded safetensors auto-prefetch when the checkpoint filesystem is reported as `virtiofs`.

The default strategy currently detects `VIRTIOFS` but leaves prefetch disabled because the automatic allowlist contains only NFS, NFS4, and Lustre. With a 1403.19 GiB GLM-5.2 checkpoint that fit within available RAM, explicit prefetch reduced model loading from 1597.0 seconds to 70.7 seconds, about 22.6x.

This change:

- adds VirtioFS to the existing automatic prefetch set;
- renames the internal network-filesystem classification because VirtioFS is a host/guest shared filesystem, not a network filesystem;
- documents default and explicit-lazy behavior;
- adds behavior coverage for VirtioFS, the RAM guard, explicit `lazy`, and a local filesystem.

### Safety and scope

Automatic prefetch still activates only when `safetensors_load_strategy` is unset and total checkpoint size is at most 90% of available RAM. Explicit `lazy` remains an opt-out.

VirtioFS backing storage, cache policy, and DAX configuration vary. The filesystem type alone does not prove that storage is high latency or that prefetched guest pages will be retained. 

This changes startup I/O scheduling only. Loaded tensor values and model outputs are unchanged.

### Duplicate check

Exact VirtioFS issue and PR searches returned no results. #47412 proposes CephFS support through the same mechanism, but only for the separate `ceph` filesystem type. This PR does not include CephFS and can rebase around #47412 if it lands first.

items.title: fix(mooncake): Restore TP replication awareness for DCP and reduce write amplification
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation

When `dcp_size > 1`, `_spec_tp_replication_factor` unconditionally returns 1, forcing every TP rank to save every chunk — `tp_size`× write amplification (e.g. 8× under TP8+DCP4). This is correct but wastes store bandwidth and capacity.

### Changes

**Restore TP replication awareness** (`worker.py`):
- Remove the `if self.dcp_size > 1: return 1` override in `_spec_tp_replication_factor`, so the true factor is used (MLA=`tp_size`, GQA=`tp_size//num_kv_head`, Mamba=1).
- Generalize `put_step` to `max(1, group_put_steps[g_idx] // dcp_size)` so each chunk is saved by exactly one rank per DCP namespace, reducing write amplification from `tp_size`× to `dcp_size`×.
- Adjust `put_step_rank` to `(tp_rank // dcp_size + g_idx) % put_step` to stripe within each DCP subgroup.

**Explicit per-rank DCP namespace** (`worker.py`, `data.py`):
- Add `dcp_size`/`dcp_rank` to `KVCacheStoreSendingThread` and `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread`.
- `key_for()` gains an optional `dcp_rank` parameter; save and load pass `dcp_rank=self.dcp_rank` so each rank writes to its own namespace.
- Restructure `_init_lookup_key_prefixes` into `(shard_rank, dcp_rank, prefix)` tuples with separate TP-shard and DCP-namespace dimensions. Add `_lookup_num_shards` for the total shard count per group.

**Safety guards** (`worker.py`):
- Clamp `token_len` to `len(block_hashes) * hash_block_size` before save (prevents `AssertionError` after external cache hit).
- Skip `NULL_BLOCK_ID` chunks during load (protects against abort races).
- Early return when all load chunks are filtered out (prevents `ZeroDivisionError`).

### Performance impact (MLA, TP8, DCP4)

| Metric | main | this PR |
|--------|------|----------|
| Write amplification | 8× per chunk | 2× per chunk |
| Lookup keys per chunk | 8 | 4 |
| Correctness | ✓ | ✓ |

### Production verification

Deployed to GLM-5.2 (TP8, DCP4, MLA): external prefix cache hit rate 28.3%, no regressions.

### Breaking changes

items.title: [Bugfix] Support NoPE models on FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 and validate effective topk buffer width
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Two fixes to the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` backend that are prerequisites for serving NoPE sparse-MLA models (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`, e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) with the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on SM120/SM121 devices such as the NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10). Related to #45317 (DSA models unable to serve on GB10).

Note on scope: the GLM-5.3-Flash model architecture itself is not upstream yet, so no in-tree model exercises these paths today with `qk_rope_head_dim=0`. These are the attention-layer fixes we needed on top of a Glm5Next-enabled build; submitting them separately so the backend is ready when the model lands, and so other GB10 users patching locally have a reference. Happy to convert to draft or fold into a larger enablement PR if maintainers prefer.

**Fix 1: NoPE models crash in `concat_and_cache_mla` (fp8_ds_mla layout assumes a rope section)**

The `fp8_ds_mla` KV-cache tile is a fixed 656-byte DeepSeek-shaped layout (512-dim fp8 latent + scales + 64-dim bf16 rope), and the compiled `concat_and_cache_mla` kernel asserts `pe_dim == 64`. Models with `qk_rope_head_dim=0` crash on that assert. This PR zero-pads the missing rope section symmetrically on both the KV-write and the query side.

Bit-exactness argument: a zero rope vector contributes exactly 0 to the `q_pe · k_pe` dot product, so attention scores are bit-for-bit identical to true NoPE. This is a layout adaptation, not a numerical approximation.

**Fix 2: support check validates raw `index_topk` instead of the effective buffer width**

The SM120 support check requires `index_topk == 2048` (the only width the FlashInfer SM120 sparse-MLA kernel is instantiated for). However, what actually reaches the kernel is the topk *buffer* width: the indexer emits `index_topk` plus up to `index_kpool - 1` always-selected tail tokens, padded up to a multiple of 128. GLM-5.3-Flash ships `index_topk=2044, index_kpool=4` → effective width 2047 → padded to 2048, which the kernel

Prevent `BuildPrefillChunkMetadataKernel` from compiling a new Triton variant during the first real sparse-MLA prefill.

The existing compile-only warmup leaves two gaps:

- request slice and decode-context-parallel scalar values are part of the compile key even though they do not change the algorithm;

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Normalize null assistant content with tool_calls
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

- Normalize assistant messages with `content: null` and `tool_calls` to use an empty string before chat templating.
- Prevents Jinja templates that render `{{ content }}` from injecting the literal string `None` into the prompt.
- Adds regression coverage in `test_chat_utils.py`.

## Problem

OpenAI agent clients (OpenAI SDK, pi, etc.) commonly send assistant turns as `content: null` plus `tool_calls`. When those messages reach `apply_chat_template`, templates that unconditionally render assistant content emit `None` as text. Over many tool-calling turns in an agent session, this silently degrades generation into repetition loops and looks like a model quality issue rather than a preprocessing bug.

Reported in #54337 with reproduction on GLM chat templates; the fix is protocol-layer and model-agnostic.

## Fix

Extend `_postprocess_messages` in `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py` to coerce `content=None` to `""` for assistant messages that include `tool_calls`, alongside the existing tool-call argument normalization.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Read the DFlash target's RoPE layout from an attention's own rotary_emb
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Purpose

`dflash_target_rope_is_neox_style` walks the target's modules and returns the
first `is_neox_style` it finds. On a NoPE target that is not the attention's
rope — it is whatever other rope the model happens to build.

GLM-5.3-Flash (#53906) is the concrete case. Its MLA attention sets
`self.rotary_emb = None` under `mla_nope`, but the sparse indexer beside it
builds `indexer_rope_emb = ...(is_neox_style=not config.indexer_rope_interleave)`.
The walk finds the indexer's rope and reports `False`, so the DFlash head is
forced to non-neox against its Qwen3 default of `True`. Nothing errors and the
output stays correct — acceptance just collapses to 1.0.

The vision tower is a second instance of the same hazard: it declares
`is_neox_style=True`, and which one the walk reaches first is incidental.

### Why no existing target hits this

Before #51655 the draft did not consult the target at all — it took the Qwen3
default from `getattr(config, "is_neox_style", True)`, which is correct for
every neox target DFlash supported. #51655 added the probe for targets with
interleaved RoPE, and on those the walk is right: their attention has a real
rope, so the first `is_neox_style` a pre-order walk reaches is the attention's.

The failure needs a target whose attention has *no* rope while the model builds
one elsewhere. GLM-5.3-Flash is the first such target.

### Fix

Read the layout off a module's own `rotary_emb` rather than off any module that
declares `is_neox_style`. A NoPE attention holds `rotary_emb = None`, which is
not a layout, so the walk runs to the end and returns `None` — the draft then
keeps the layout it was distilled with.

```diff
-        style = getattr(module, "is_neox_style", None)
+        style = getattr(getattr(module, "rotary_emb", None), "is_neox_style", None)
```

Inside `get_language_model()` every rope in the tree is named `rotary_emb` (89
sites); the two other names, `rotary_pos_emb` and `rotary_embedding`, belong to
vision and audio encod

items.title: [Feature] Support downloading models from AtomGit
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Add **AtomGit** as a third model download source, alongside HuggingFace and ModelScope, mirroring the `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE` UX:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT=True
vllm serve hf_mirrors/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --served-model-name Qwen3.8-27B ...
```

- When `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT=True`, redirects `HF_ENDPOINT` to `https://hub.atomgit.com` early at import time (`vllm/env_override.py`), matching what the `atomgit_hub` SDK does on import; vLLM's existing HuggingFace download paths (config / tokenizer / weights / processors) work unchanged.
- Repo ids with 3+ path segments (e.g. `hf_mirrors/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`) are normalized to the 2-segment form (`hf_mirrors-Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`) in `ModelConfig`, consistent with the atomgit SDK's `_normalize_repo_id`; 2-segment ids (e.g. `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`) are kept as-is.
- Reuses the token saved by `atomgit login` (`~/.atomgit/config.json`) as `HF_TOKEN`, exported only when the endpoint actually points at AtomGit so the credential is never sent to a third-party endpoint; robust against malformed config (non-dict JSON / non-string token) so `import vllm` never crashes.
- Normalization skips URLs, object-storage URIs (`s3://`, `gs://`, `az://`, `runai://`, ...) and absolute/relative paths, so existing features such as RunAI object storage are unaffected; when both `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE` and `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT` are set, AtomGit takes precedence.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched open PRs of vllm-project/vllm via the GitHub search API for `AtomGit`, `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT`, `atomgit download` and `atomgit in:title` — all returned 0 results. No duplicate PR exists.

## Test commands run and results

- `uvx ruff check` (all changed files + test file): **all pass**
- New unit test `tests/transformers_utils/test_utils.py::test_normalize_atomgit_repo_id`: covers 1/2/3/4-segment ids and exclusion of URLs / object-storage URIs / absolute paths
- Verified against the real `hub.atomgit.com` endpoint:
